paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
research_problem: Large language models often produce responses containing factual inaccuracies due to sole reliance on parametric knowledge; while retrieval-augmented generation can mitigate this, indiscriminately retrieving and incorporating a fixed number of passages regardless of necessity or relevance diminishes versatility or leads to unhelpful generations.

subgoals.label: adaptive retrieval on-demand
subgoals.description: Decide when retrieval is needed instead of always retrieving a fixed number of passages.
subgoals.success_criterion: The model produces reflection tokens indicating whether retrieval is required and only retrieves passages when necessary, with empirical evaluation on tasks where retrieval decisions affect output quality.
subgoals.rationale: Trains a single LM that generates special reflection tokens (Retrieve, IsRel, IsSup, IsUse) to decide when and how to retrieve and use passages; experiments show gains over fixed-retrieval baselines on QA, reasoning and fact verification.

subgoals.label: self-reflection on retrieved passages and generations
subgoals.description: Generate reflection tokens that critique relevance, support, and usefulness of retrieved content and own output.
subgoals.success_criterion: The LM emits reflection tokens during generation that allow controllable behavior and measurable improvement in factuality or citation accuracy.
subgoals.rationale: Reflection tokens are trained and used at inference; results report significant gains in factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generation relative to ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat.

subgoals.label: versatility across diverse task requirements
subgoals.description: Tailor retrieval and generation behavior at inference time without retraining for different tasks.
subgoals.success_criterion: Single trained model outperforms strong baselines on a diverse set of tasks (open-domain QA, reasoning, fact verification, long-form generation) via controllable reflection-token behavior.
subgoals.rationale: Experiments demonstrate that the same 7B/13B models outperform ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat across the listed task categories.

dropped_candidates.label: general robustness or scalability beyond reported model sizes
dropped_candidates.reason: Specificity: too generic paraphrase of overall problem; no concrete success criterion tied to a distinct measurable condition was stated in the problem framing.
